newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva private bank overweight in Brazil, Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Geneva private bank overweight in Brazil, Mexico.

text.p: Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee's equities portfolio is overweight in Brazil and Mexico in Latin America and in France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands in Europe, its latest market outlook said on Monday.
The Geneva bank said it was particularly bullish about Brazil thanks to a favourable international financial climate.
The bank's overall equities portfolio was overweight in Europe and underweight in the Asian Pacific region.

Assets allocated in Asia favoured Hong Kong, Singapore and Thailand and were underweight in Malaysia, Australia, South Korea and Japan, where the bank cautioned against an April increase in sales tax which it said would hit consumer spending.
Shares in Hong Kong make up about four percent of the bank's stock portfolio.

In Europe, the bank said it was a buyer of shares of Societe Generale in France and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya and Bankinter in Spain, where it saw bright prospects for the stock market -- now on a valuation of 15 times projected 1997 earnings and enjoying a return of Spanish investors.
Union Bancaire Privee's medium-risk dollar portfolio allocations were unchanged from late 1996 with roughly 45 percent in equities and stocks, 30 in bonds and 25 in cash.
Its medium-risk Swiss franc portfolio allocated 45 percent in equities, 45 percent in bonds and 10 percent in cash.
